newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen under pressure to open weaker.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen under pressure to open weaker.

text.p: * Toronto stocks were likely to extend Thursday's weakness into Friday's open, pushed lower by softer bonds and golds.
* Double-witching seen keeping equities markets volatile.
Toronto's key stock index was seen opening softer on Friday, extending Thursday's modest losses, pressured by weaker bond markets and gold stocks.
"The short-term trend is to the down side," said MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie. On Thursday, the Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index fell 24.17 points to 6766.85.
Canada's benchmark 30-year bond dropped C$0.56 to C$119.03 to yield 6.54 percent, while gold bullion prices eased.
Investors also face the volatility of double-witching, the expiry of options and futures, which occurs every two months.
